module: Common toolbox (GE and vehicle) loaded at the startup of each Lua VM. This file does not return a table M: it directly defines hundreds of GLOBAL functions (dump, deepcopy, tableMerge, jsonReadFile, jsonWriteFile, readFile, split, colors, serialization, etc.), extends the `string` library (string.startswith, string.split...), creates the global table `path` and assigns the global `lpack`. A modder calls them directly, without require. It also loads `filters`, `inputFilters`, `lpack` and `libs/inspect/inspect`.
notes: File paths are those of the game's virtual file system (e.g. '/settings/...', '/levels/...') or disk paths for io.open.
Colors: color(r,g,b,a) returns a 32-bit RGBA integer (r*2^24 + g*2^16 + b*2^8 + a), components 0..255; hueColor/jetColor/ironbowColor/greyColor take x in [0..1].
tableSize/tableDepth/deepcopy are slow (they walk the whole table): avoid them in a per-frame loop.

Many functions return a shared buffer (jsonEncodeWorkBuffer, serializeWorkBuffer, concatWorkBuffer, stringFormatWorkBuffer): the content is overwritten on the next call, so it must be converted (tostring) immediately.
jsonEncode and jsonEncodeWorkBuffer share the same internal buffer as serialize: do not nest these calls.
Bug/inconsistency: getCurrentLevelIdentifier(raw) -> the raw parameter changes nothing (the result of string.gsub is ignored when raw is true, the returned value is always lowercase).

Bug/inconsistency: concatWorkBuffer, in the table branch, tests `vtype == 'boolean'` instead of `vtype1` and puts `v` (the table) instead of `v1` in the buffer for non-numeric elements: this raises an error if an element of the table is not a number.
Bug/inconsistency: dumpToFile calls inspect(...) with all the arguments: the optional second argument is interpreted as the inspect options table, not as a second value to write.
Inconsistency: arrayFindValueIndex returns false (and not nil) when the value is absent.
Inconsistency: saveIni returns nothing (neither true nor false), whereas loadIni returns nil on failure.
Inconsistency: string.rstripchars and string.stripchars return two values (the result of gsub: text then number of replacements).
Inconsistency: dump and dumpz log with level 'A' and origin 'lua.utils'; dumpNotNil goes through Lua:log with an empty origin.
The commented-out code `pairs = sortedPairs` at the bottom of the file shows how to make pairs loops deterministic (the real pairs function is kept in the local `unsortedPairs`).

RGBtoHSV.desc: Converts an RGB color to HSV. The r,g,b inputs are in [0..1] (inferred from code: no 255 scaling).

HSVtoRGB.desc: Converts an HSV color to RGB, components in [0..1].

color.desc: Builds a 32-bit RGBA color integer. Each component is rounded down to the integer and clamped to 0..255.

colorGetRGBA.desc: Inverse operation of color(): decomposes an RGBA integer.

colorHex.desc: Builds an RGBA color integer from an RGB hexadecimal (e.g. 0xff8800) and an alpha.

tableToColor.desc: Converts a table {r,g,b,a} (0..255) into a color integer. Returns 0 if the table is nil.

v.desc: Table with the fields r, g, b, a

parseColor.desc: Converts to a color integer a table {r,g,b,a}, a string '#RRGGBBAA' (at least 8 characters with the #) or nil (gives transparent 0,0,0,0). Any other type returns nil.

returns.desc: 32-bit RGBA color, nil if the format is not recognized

hueColor.desc: Color from the full hue spectrum (maximum saturation and value). Useful for indexed colors: hueColor(indexedBlueNoise(i)).

rainbowColor.desc: Rainbow color for step `step` out of numOfSteps. The code recommends jetColor instead unless there is a reason not to.

format.desc: 255 (default) for integer components 0..255, any other value for [0..1] components

returns.desc: {r,g,b,a} (a is 255 or 1 depending on the format)

jetColor.desc: Color from the 'jet' palette (blue, green, red). Recommended default palette for visualizing a value.

dumps.desc: Returns the text representation (via libs/inspect) of the arguments, separated by ', '. With no arguments returns ''. For a single userdata with a metatable, inspects the metatable.

dump.desc: Prints to the log (level 'A', origin 'lua.utils') the result of dumps(...). The most common debug function for inspecting a table.

dumpsz.desc: Like inspect but with unlimited depth by default (depth = math.huge).

dumpz.desc: Prints to the log (level 'A', origin 'lua.utils') the result of dumpsz(o, depth).

dumpNotNil.desc: Like dump, but prints nothing if x is nil (and takes only one value).

x.desc: Value to print if not nil

addLevelLog.desc: Adds an entry to the engine level log (Engine.Debug.addLevelLogLua), with the caller's file and line (debug.getinfo(2)). Without an object, uses addLevelLogLuaNoObject.

object.desc: Object to attach the log to, nil for none

logLevel.desc: Log level (passed as is to the engine)

uniqueErrorCode.desc: Unique error code (passed to the engine)

returns.desc: Engine result (inferred from code: list of logs)

lpad.desc: Pads s on the left with the character c up to length l. s is converted by tostring.

returns.desc: Padded text (unchanged if already long enough)

rpad.desc: Pads s on the right with the character c up to length l. s is converted by tostring.

trim.desc: Removes spaces at the start and end of a string.

returns.desc: String without spaces at the ends

split.desc: Splits str on the delimiter delim (plain text search, not a regex). An empty string returns an empty array. Empty fields are kept.

nMax.desc: Maximum number of splits (default -1 = unlimited); the rest of the string goes into the last element

stringHash.desc: Computes a numeric hash of a string (StringHash algorithm from the WoW wiki).

bytes_to_string.desc: Converts a number of bytes to readable text with 2 decimals. Uses powers of 1000 (KB, MB, GB), not 1024.

formatTimeStringNow.desc: Replaces in res the current local date/time tokens: {YYYY} {YY} {Y} {MM} {M} {DD} {D} {HH} {H} {mm} {m} {ss} {s} (the doubled forms use 2 digits, YYYY uses 4).

graphs.desc: Builds a small ASCII chart of a value: '[' + len signs (+ or - depending on the sign of v) + spaces + ']'.

v.desc: Value (only the integer part of |v| counts)

len.desc: Width of the gauge in characters

jsonEncodeWorkBuffer.desc: Encodes a value as JSON into a shared string.buffer (without copying into a string). Infinite/NaN numbers are written as 9e999 / -9e999; vec3/quat (cdata) become {x,y,z[,w]}; unsupported types become null. A table that has key 1 is written as an array.

returns.desc: Shared buffer (overwritten on the next call)

jsonEncode.desc: Encodes a Lua value as compact JSON text.

jsonEncodePrefix.desc: Encodes v as compact JSON, preceded by prefix and optionally followed by postfix.

jsonEncodePretty.desc: Encodes as indented JSON (2 spaces per level), object keys sorted. Recursive.

numberPrecision.desc: If given, non-integer numbers are written with this number of decimals (format %N.Nf); nil = tostring

jsonDecode.desc: Decodes JSON (json module) inside an xpcall. On error, logs the context and the error and returns nil.

context.desc: Text (often the file name) shown in the error message

jsonWriteFile.desc: Writes a table to a JSON file. Refuses (log E + false) if obj is not a table. With atomicWrite, writes to a temporary file first and then renames it (FS:renameFile).

atomicWrite.desc: Truthy: atomic write via a temporary file; if it is a string, it is used as the temporary file name, otherwise filename..'.tmp'

jsonReadFile.desc: Reads and decodes a JSON file. Returns nil if the file is unreadable (no log: the caller handles the error) or if the JSON is invalid (log E by jsonDecode).

readDictJSONTable.desc: Reads a JSON of 'headers + rows' arrays: for each entry, the first row gives the column names, and each following row is turned into a named table; the header row is then removed (v[1] = nil).

returns.desc: Transformed data, nil if the read is impossible

setEqual.desc: Tests whether two arrays contain the same values (length comparison, then membership; ignores order).

setUnion.desc: Adds to dst all values of src that are absent from dst (modifies dst).

setDifference.desc: Removes from dst all values present in src. Modifies dst and changes the order of its elements.

concatWorkBuffer.desc: Concatenates the arguments (numbers, strings, booleans, or arrays of numbers) into a shared buffer. Stops at the first nil argument. Infinite/NaN numbers are written as 9e999 / -9e999.

returns.desc: Shared buffer (overwritten on the next call)

stringFormatWorkBuffer.desc: Equivalent of string.format written into a shared buffer (buffer:putf), without string allocation.

tableIsDict.desc: Returns true if tbl is a table whose first element does not have key 1 (quick test: next(tbl) ~= 1). An empty table therefore counts as a dictionary. Returns false if it is not a table.

tableIsArraySlow.desc: Strictly checks that all keys are integers from 1 to #tbl with no gaps. Walks the whole table.

tableIsEmpty.desc: Returns true if tbl is not a table or if it is empty.

returns.desc: true if empty or not a table

tableKeys.desc: Returns an array of all keys of tbl (order undefined).

tableKeysSorted.desc: Like tableKeys, but sorted. The sort accepts mixed types: first by type name, then by value (numbers, strings), true booleans first, others by tostring.

tableValuesAsLookupDict.desc: Builds a value -> 1 dictionary from the values of tbl, to test membership in O(1).

arrayConcat.desc: Appends to the end of dst all elements of the array src (includes index 0 of src if it exists). Modifies dst.

tableMerge.desc: Copies all key/value pairs from src into dst (overwrites existing keys, non-recursive).

tableMergeRecursive.desc: Recursive merge of the sub-tables of t2 into t1. Warning: arrays are not concatenated, their elements overwrite each other by index.

tableMergeRecursiveArray.desc: Recursive merge that concatenates pure arrays (instead of overwriting them) and merges associative tables. Tables absent from t1 are copied.

tableSize.desc: Counts the entries of a table (array or dictionary) by walking it entirely. Returns 0 for a non-table.

tableReadOnly.desc: Returns a read-only proxy table (__index metatable pointing to the original; any write raises an error). Only the first level is protected.

tableSizeC.desc: Size of an array, also counting the element at index 0 (C convention) if it exists.

tableEndC.desc: Returns the index at which to insert the next element in a 0-based array: 0 if the table is empty, otherwise #tbl + 1.

tableInsertC.desc: Inserts data at the end of a 0-based array: at tbl[0] if index 0 is free, otherwise table.insert.

tableFindKey.desc: Returns the first key associated with the value element (non-recursive, pairs order).

tableContains.desc: Tests whether the table contains the value element (non-recursive).

tableContainsCaseInsensitive.desc: Tests whether the table contains the string element, ignoring case. The table values must be strings.

arrayFindValueIndex.desc: Returns the index of the first occurrence of val in the array t.

returns.desc: Index, or false (not nil) if absent

arrayShuffle.desc: Shuffles a pure array in place (Fisher-Yates, math.random).

arrayReverse.desc: Reverses a pure array in place.

tableDepth.desc: Computes the nesting depth of a table (table keys and values). Recursive and very slow; 0 for a non-table.

tableRoundRobinKey.desc: Iterates cyclically over the keys: returns the key following lastKey, or the first key if the end is reached or lastKey is nil/absent.

lastKey.desc: Key returned by the previous call

returns.desc: Next key (nil if the table is empty)

shallowcopy.desc: Non-recursive copy of a table (sub-tables remain shared). Non-table values are returned as is. The metatable is not copied.

deepcopy.desc: Recursive copy of a table, handling circular/shared references and keeping the metatable. FFI structures (vec3, quat) are shallow-copied. Slow.

checkTableDataTypes.desc: Validates the types of a parameter array. Prefix an expected type with 'optional:' to allow nil. Pure arrays only.

returns.desc: Error message if invalid (too many parameters or wrong type)

dumpToFile.desc: Writes to a file the text inspect(...) of the argument.

....desc: Value to inspect (see notes: the 2nd argument is read as inspect options)

returns.desc: true if the file was written, false if it could not be opened

readFile.desc: Reads the whole content of a text file (io.open in mode 'r', with profiler event 'readFile').

returns.desc: Content, nil if the file does not exist or cannot be opened

writeFile.desc: Writes text to a file (mode 'w', overwrites). If opening fails, logs a warning.

returns.desc: true if written, nil if it could not be opened

ui_message.desc: Shows an on-screen message via guihooks.message. Shortcut used by many scripts.

ttl.desc: Display duration in seconds, 5 by default

ui_toast.desc: Shows a 'toast' notification in the UI (UI event toastrMsg).

fillActionLabelSimple.desc: From a list of action names, builds {action=...} and then calls fillActionLabels.

fillActionLabels.desc: For each item {action=...}, sets `missing` (true if the action is not active in core_input_actions) and `label` (the action's title, or its name if absent) if label is nil.

actionItems.desc: List of items with the action field

serializePackages.desc: Collects the state to keep before a Lua reload: for each loaded package defining onSerialize or onDeserialized, calls onSerialize(reason), otherwise takes M.state, otherwise M. Adds the extensions data (extensions.getSerializationData). Errors are logged and ignored. Called by the engine during reloads.

reason.desc: Reason for the reload, 'reload' by default

deserializePackages.desc: Restores the state produced by serializePackages: calls extensions.deserialize, then for each concerned package calls onDeserialize(data) or merges the data (excluding functions) into M.state or M, then calls onDeserialized(data).

filter.desc: If given, restores only that package

getCurrentLevelIdentifier.desc: Returns the identifier (folder) of the current level in lowercase, inferred from the path of getMissionFilename() under /levels/. Returns nil if the path has no folder.

getAllLevelIdentifiers.desc: Lists the folders under /levels/ (FS:findFiles) and returns their names in lowercase.

loadIni.desc: Reads a simple INI file (key = value, no sections). Ignores empty lines and those starting with #, ; or /. Converts values to number or boolean when possible; an unreadable line is logged as an error.

returns.desc: Key/value pairs, nil if the file cannot be opened

saveIni.desc: Writes a simple INI: 3 header comment lines (window title, game version, date), then the sorted keys in 'key = value' format.

serializeWorkBuffer.desc: Serializes a value as Lua code (reloadable by deserialize) into a shared buffer. Handles _noSerialize (writes nil), _serialize (table or true: restricts or not the keys, format _kv{...}), QuatF (userdata), cdata (tostring). Functions become nil.

returns.desc: Shared buffer (overwritten on the next call)

serialize.desc: Serializes a value as Lua text that deserialize() can read back.

_kv.desc: Helper used by the text produced by serialize: builds a table from a flat list {k1, v1, k2, v2…}. A modder normally does not need to call it.

kv.desc: Flat list key, value, key, value…

deserialize.desc: Reads back text produced by serialize() by executing loadstring('return '..s). Returns nil if s is nil. Crashes if the text is not valid Lua (e.g. non-serializable cdata).

detectGlobalWrites.desc: Debug tool: installs a metatable on _G that logs (level W, with trace) every creation of a new global variable.

gcprobe.desc: Measures the bytes of garbage created between two calls. First call: stops the GC and remembers the memory. Second call: restarts the GC, prints (if > 0 or printZero) and returns the difference.

printZero.desc: Also print when the difference is 0

timeprobeStart.desc: Always starts a timer (os.clockhp), even if a timeprobe was already running.

timeprobe.desc: First call: starts the timer. Second call: prints the duration in milliseconds and returns it in seconds.

jitprobe.desc: Toggles the JIT compiler trace (jit.v): enabled on the first call, disabled on the next.

flattenTable.desc: Replaces in tbl, in place, multiple references to the same sub-table with a text token '>#>/path' (to serialize graphs). Keys are walked in sorted order.

returns.desc: tbl, or nil if it is not a table

unflattenTable.desc: Inverse of flattenTable: replaces the '>#>/path' tokens with the original sub-tables. Logs an error if the link does not exist.

returns.desc: tbl, or nil if it is not a table

sortedPairs.desc: Like pairs but in sorted key order (mixed types accepted, or sort function f). Keys are frozen at the start; a value set to nil during the loop is skipped.

ctx.desc: Reusable working table to avoid allocations

shuffledPairs.desc: Like pairs but in random order.

hex_dump.desc: Prints (print) a hexadecimal dump of a string, 8 bytes per line with the ASCII column.

objectTeleported.desc: Decides whether an object teleported between two frames, based on its previous position and velocity. No teleport if the displacement is less than 1.5 m or 277*dt (1000 km/h), or if the velocity is consistent with the previous one. Without previous data, returns true.

simpleDebugText3d.desc: Draws via debugDrawer a 3D text, a sphere and/or three small axis spheres oriented by dir.

radius.desc: Sphere radius (m), nothing if nil or <= 0

dir.desc: Orientation: draws the X (red), Y (green), Z (blue) axes at distance radius

string.startswith.desc: Added to the string library: true if String starts with Start. Usable as String:startswith(Start).

string.endswith.desc: Added to string: true if String ends with End (an empty End always gives true).

string.rstripchars.desc: Added to string: removes from the end of the text ONE character from the set chrs (gsub with the class [chrs]$). chrs is inserted into a Lua character class.

string.stripchars.desc: Added to string: removes everywhere in the text the characters of the set chrs.

string.stripcharsFrontBack.desc: Added to string: removes at the start and at the end the characters of the set chrs.

string.split.desc: Added to string: splits by returning all matches of the pattern delimregex (string.gmatch). Warning: the pattern describes the PIECES to keep, not the separator. Default '%S+' (words separated by spaces). Different from the global function split.

delimregex.desc: Lua pattern of the pieces, '%S+' by default

string.sentenceCase.desc: Added to string: inserts a space before each capital letter then capitalizes the first letter (e.g. 'maVariable' becomes 'Ma Variable').

path.desc: Global table `path` defined in this file: file path utilities (separator '/').

dirname.desc: Returns the folder of a path, with the trailing '/' ('.' if no folder).

is_file.desc: Tests whether the file can be opened for reading (io.open).

split.desc: Splits a path into folder, file name (WITH extension) and extension. Without an extension, ext is ''.

compositeExtension.desc: true: the extension is everything after the first dot of the name (e.g. 'level.json')

returns.desc: Folder with trailing '/' (nil for a simple file name)

splitWithoutExt.desc: Like split but the returned file name has no extension. Warning: removes it via gsub('.'..ext) (the dot is a pattern wildcard).

getCurrentPath.desc: Returns the folder of the caller's Lua file (debug.getinfo(2).short_src).

getPathLevelMain.desc: Path of a level's main.level.json file, normalized by sanitizePath.

getPathLevelInfo.desc: Path of a level's info.json file, normalized by sanitizePath.

levelFromPath.desc: Extracts from a path the level name (under 'levels/') and the rest of the path.
